doc.title: Ray Conniff interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998

title: First conducting and hit arrangements for Miller's artists
summary: Conniff sets tempos for the first time, then arranges hits for Don Cherry, Johnnie Ray, Johnny Mathis and Marty Robbins with whistle and piano hooks.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: got a conductor, I’ll bring the arrangements in and give them to him. So this was the first time. Up to now in my career, I’m bringing arrangements, giving them to Harry James, he’s setting the tempo. I’m giving them to Artie Shaw, he’s setting the tempos. I’m not up there. So this is the first time I come in with two charts, and I set the tempos, I tell them how to play them, I go in the booth and tell them how to balance them. And so Mitch was tickled to death. He thought this is great. This guy is great. So he started giving me all his artists. I did Don Cherry’s “Band of Gold,” do you remember that a little later? Then I did Johnnie Ray “Just Walking in the Rain.” And by the way, Dick Hyman did the whistling on that. That had a little hook in it, the whistle. And I did “Singing the Blues” with the through-the-teeth whistle like Haggart does? I did the whistle on “Singing the Blues.” And I did the early Johnny Mathis’ “Chances Are” it’s not for me to say, with the piano hook. [scats].
Sounds like whoever did “I Left My Heart in San Francisco” must have heard that recording.
